questions.prompt: The tribune of the plebs defended the rights of the citizens with great courage.
questions.answer: Tribūnus plēbis iūra cīvium magnā virtūte dēfendit.

questions.prompt: The son of the king, worthy of friendship, ruled the neighboring peoples justly.
questions.answer: Fīlius rēgis, dignus amīcitiā, populōs fīnitimōs iūstē rēxit.

questions.prompt: A man of noble spirit does not fear the threats of enemies.
questions.answer: Vir magnī animī minās hostium nōn timet.

questions.prompt: The young man, ignorant of affairs, scorned the counsel of wise men.
questions.answer: Adulēscēns, ignārus rērum, cōnsilium sapientium sprēvit.

questions.prompt: Philip, king of the Macedonians, waged war against the Greeks for many years.
questions.answer: Philippus, rēx Macedonum, bellum contrā Graecōs multōs annōs gessit.

questions.prompt: The river Rhine separates the Gauls from the fierce Germans.
questions.answer: Flūmen Rhēnus Gallōs ā ferōcibus Germānīs sēparat.

questions.prompt: We saw the city Rome, mistress of the whole world.
questions.answer: Urbem Rōmam, tōtīus orbis dominam, vīdimus.

questions.prompt: Hear, Caesar, the just complaints of the soldiers!
questions.answer: Audī, Caesar, iūstās mīlitum querēlās!

questions.prompt: Spare, o gods, the city besieged by cruel enemies.
questions.answer: Parcite, dī, urbī ab hostibus crūdēlibus obsessae.

questions.prompt: Tell me, faithful friend, the counsels of the leaders.
questions.answer: Dīc mihi, amīce fidēlis, cōnsilia ducum.

questions.prompt: Do not fear, soldiers, the great multitude of the enemy.
questions.answer: Nōlīte timēre, mīlitēs, magnam hostium multitūdinem.

questions.prompt: All the men praised the courage of the young leader.
questions.answer: Omnēs hominēs virtūtem ducis adulēscentis laudāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Seven hundred ships carried the soldiers of the king across the sea.
questions.answer: Septingentae nāvēs mīlitēs rēgis trāns mare portāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Many citizens feared the power of the new consul.
questions.answer: Multī cīvēs potestātem cōnsulis novī timēbant.

questions.prompt: Both armies awaited the arrival of the general with great fear.
questions.answer: Ambō exercitūs adventum imperātōris magnō metū exspectābant.

questions.prompt: The veterans, worthy of praise, returned to their homeland.
questions.answer: Veterānī, dignī laude, in patriam revertērunt.

questions.prompt: The philosophers, eager for truth, despised the pleasures of the body.
questions.answer: Philosophī, cupidī veritātis, voluptātēs corporis contempsērunt.

questions.prompt: Full of wisdom, the old man taught the sons of the nobles.
questions.answer: Plēnus sapientiae, senex fīliōs nōbilium docēbat.

questions.prompt: Mindful of his duty, the consul feared nothing more than disgrace.
questions.answer: Cōnsul, memor officiī, nihil magis quam turpitūdinem timēbat.

questions.prompt: Cicero, defender of the state, condemned the crimes of Catiline.
questions.answer: Cicerō, dēfēnsor cīvitātis, scelera Catilīnae culpāvit.

questions.prompt: Listen, judges, to the words of the truthful witness.
questions.answer: Audīte, iūdicēs, verba testis vēridicī.

questions.prompt: All the citizens admired the calm face of the stoic teacher.
questions.answer: Omnēs cīvēs placidum vultum magistrī stoicī mīrābantur.

questions.prompt: Cyrus, king of the Persians, overcame many peoples of Asia.
questions.answer: Cȳrus, rēx Persārum, multās Asiae gentēs superāvit.
